correctness.rationale: With unit rim conductances and spoke conductance r=2(cosh(a)-1), grounded rim Laplacian rI+Delta(C_m) has explicit positive Green inverse g_k=C(t^k+t^{m-k}), t=e^-a. From it hub resistance alpha and rim resistances delta_k=2alpha(1-Q_mk). The squared rim-distance circulant has strictly negative Fourier eigenvalues for every nonconstant rim mode by an exact strictly signed rational expression. On total zero-sum coefficients, split into rim contrasts z and radial hub contrast s: z^TD_rim²z+2s²(alpha² H_m-alpha²). Hence unique obstruction H_m(a)<=1, critical equality vector (m,-1,...,-1), dimensions m and m-1, and one negative centered Gram eigenvalue above. Monotonicity of cosh-ratios makes H_m strictly increase from 0 to 2(m-1)/m>1. The finite-metric negative-type interval property yields the three generalized-roundness regimes, and Riemann-sum H_m(c/m) -> explicit integral gives m²r_m -> 34.847671295...; m=3 root 3+2sqrt3. All parameters m>=3,r>0 are addressed.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for Euclidean embeddability of *resistance distance itself* on a weighted wheel, its sharp spoke threshold, critical kernel/inertia, generalized-roundness regimes and inverse-square scaling. Bapat–Gupta Theorem 5 already gives exact weighted wheel resistance entries and is fully credited; it does not study the squared resistance as a Euclidean-distance-matrix condition. General p-negative type tests and cycle resistance identities do not explicitly supply the wheel hub radial threshold or continuum constant. Possible implicit derivation from complete weighted resistance matrix and Schoenberg criterion is a residual priority concern, but nontrivial Fourier sign and boundary/symmetry analysis are performed here.
residual_risks: The weighted wheel resistance entries are established, not new, and may allow an earlier implicit embedding classification through general finite-metric criteria.
Generalized roundness away from r_m is only localized relative to exponent 2; no explicit formula for wp(m,r) at general r is claimed.
